inputs.original_text: The apology is just cover: make parents feel guilty while the people directing things stay hidden. More than 70 school positions are on the chopping block, and they’re calling another shortfall unavoidable—as if these repeated crises have no cause. This looks like a managed pressure campaign to get the public to accept cuts without questioning who set these priorities or who benefits from keeping schools under strain.
inputs.modified_text: That apology is a distraction, designed to make parents feel responsible while the people setting the agenda stay out of sight. More than 70 school positions are on the chopping block, and another “unavoidable” shortfall is being presented as if nobody made choices that led here. It looks like a pressure campaign: keep schools strained, then use the crisis to make cuts seem inevitable and discourage people from asking who benefits.
